claims.statement: spike_w3/predictor.py implements the T3 rolling predictor as module-level pure functions (rem_of, a_of, predict, obs_window, build_takt_baseline) plus the AlphaTracker class, with no hidden prediction state; the W2 module 02_replay_shift is referenced read-only via importlib because its numeric filename cannot be imported normally.

predictor.rem_of computes a vehicle's remaining seconds as ETA − last_event_ts and dispatches across three estimator generations by env gates: DSS_DUAL_RING=1 → eta_v2.estimate_event_unified (mode='shift', with passed_oven/loop_exited/entry_shift), DSS_DUAL_RING=0 + DSS_USE_NET_DELAY=1 → estimate_event_net_delay, otherwise estimate_event; an unresolvable distribution returns None (the no-ETA bucket, counted but never predicted), and the week label is the ISO week of the anchor date t.date().

The rem returned by rem_of is full-caliber (base + delay, including net delay) and alpha is applied exactly once at the predict() consumption point as rem/alpha (single scaling point); it is never re-scaled inside the estimator, and predict never scales A(t) because A is an already-occurred fact.

predictor.a_of counts A(t) = distinct product bodies (BODY_ID LIKE '78202%') with an exit event at any of the 4 EXIT_STATIONS in the closed interval [shift.attr_start, t] via COUNT(DISTINCT BODY_ID); the closed interval means an exit at exactly 16:30:00 counts to both the day shift (t=end inclusive) and the mid shift (attr_start inclusive), matching the W2 static exit_arr source constructively. It intentionally does not use the pool (which removes cars at exit, R3, with no exit timestamp), and the window is bounded (≤ ~12h, ~12ms per real query).

predictor.predict computes pred(t) = A(t) + count of in-process cars v with t + rem_v/alpha <= shift.end; the in-process set is pool.snapshot() intersect product cars (body_id starting with '78202'), non-product sentinel cars are excluded from the count and the by_vehicle detail, no-ETA cars are excluded from pred but visible, and stale cars ((t − last_event_ts) > eta_stale_hours) are flagged in the detail but still counted in pred to preserve alpha=off consistency with the static replay (which has no stale exclusion). It returns {shift_id, t, A, inproc, pred, no_eta, stale, by_vehicle} and raises ValueError when t < shift.attr_start.

predictor.obs_window returns the alpha observation window [max(t−window, attr_start), min(t, end−30min)] with its length in hours; it returns None when t >= shift.end or t < attr_start or the clipped length is < 1h. The end−30min pin removes the pre-closing 30-minute tail (B5) so alpha never reacts to the final-moment stop; the production Phase-1 line-stop exclusion set is an empty reserved slot.

predictor.build_takt_baseline computes, at boot via a single SQL aggregate with no new table, the per-(shift-kind, shift-type) P50 hourly product-car exit rate as the alpha denominator: per-day types come from detect_day_type/detect_mid_type applied to a pure historical window (no future leakage), exit events are attributed by hour bucket (05:00–15:59 → same-day day type; ≥16h → same-day mid; ≤4h → previous-day mid), type-None days are dropped, and n_hours < min_samples triggers a fallback to the nearest work-hour shift type (same kind); if still insufficient the type has no baseline and alpha stays 1.0 with a no_baseline flag. It returns {(kind, type): (p50_rate, n_hours, source)} with source 'direct' or 'fallback_<other>'.

AlphaTracker is a pure (no-DB) EMA state machine with window_hours=3.0, ema_beta=0.3, and clamp [0.6, 1.5]; each update computes raw = (exits_in_window/window_hours)/p50_rate, clamps raw immediately to [0.6,1.5], then ema = beta*raw + (1-beta)*ema_prev, and committed advances to ema only when (ema − committed) keeps the same sign with |Δ| >= 0.05 for 2 consecutive cycles (a +0.06/−0.06 oscillation never commits). on_shift resets committed=1.0, ema=None, and clears hysteresis counters while binding the (kind,type) baseline; a missing baseline type leaves alpha permanently 1.0. The hysteresis threshold 0.05 and 2 cycles are code-level constants (HYST_THRESHOLD/HYST_CYCLES), deliberately not env-configured.

The production default is DSS_ALPHA_MODE=off, fixed by the 2026-09-25 decision and recorded in docs/04 (alpha gate baseline; G2 judged on the alpha=off median, G3 true and G4 softened because alpha is not enabled) and in .env.example; DSSConfig.alpha_mode defaults to 'off' with DSS_ALPHA_MODE the only on/off gate. With off, alpha is fixed at 1.0 across predict and the alert engine and the tracker is not advanced into the prediction path.

alert_engine.split_target implements the M2 hour-ratio formula: day share = H_day/(H_day+H_mid) with largest-remainder rounding so the day+mid targets sum exactly to total (day takes floor, mid takes the remainder); a rest/0/missing side contributes 0 work-hours (single-side rest → the other side gets all of total), and both sides empty or total=0 yields (0,0). plan_loader.WeeklyPlan.plan_target delegates to this same function, making it the single target source shared by the dashboard, the alert engine, and the M9/M10 gates.

grade(delta, cfg) maps Δ = (pred−target)/target to 'red' when Δ <= cfg.alert_red, 'yellow' when alert_red < Δ <= alert_yellow, and 'green' otherwise (boundaries inclusive). The thresholds are the 2026-09-23 user decision preserved in .env.example: DSS_ALERT_RED=-0.10 (red at Δ ≤ −10%), DSS_ALERT_YELLOW=-0.05 (yellow at −10% < Δ ≤ −5%), and DSS_ALERT_DEBOUNCE_MIN=10; DSSConfig defaults mirror them (-0.10/-0.05/10).

Debouncer confirms a level transition only after it persists for debounce_min (default 10) physical minutes, judged by (t − pending_since) >= timedelta(minutes=debounce_min) on aware timestamps: the first level (initial state) confirms immediately as a prev_level=None baseline record; same-level or flash-back-to-current clears the pending state; a third level restarts the timer; and after a confirmation the same level does not re-fire. At a 5-minute step this is detect at step 0, pending at 5min, confirm at 10min (3 samples).

AlertEngine.evaluate evaluates two scopes per 5-minute step: (1) the shift scope for each active shift (attr_start <= t < end) with a plan entry of total>0, targeting the split_target share for that side, pred = a_fn + hit from _split_pool(by_vehicle, t, shift.end, alpha); and (2) the day_total scope, the whole-day main view, evaluated ONLY while a mid shift is active ([16:30, next-day 04:00), the F10 activation decision) using A_all = a_fn from the done day shift (attribution window [04:45, t] ⊇ mid window, union counted once) and the later end-of-day (max of the day's shift ends) as scope_end, targeting the full-day total. No scope is produced for rest/stop/missing-plan days or target<=0 (no Δ, guarding division by zero).

The alert engine self-computes pred from pred_fn's by_vehicle only and deliberately does not trust the predictor's scalar A/pred fields, so an erroneous predictor scalar cannot propagate into alerts (M9 error-isolation, F9); consuming the shared by_vehicle also means zero new pool queries per step. pred_fn returns the M9 predict() shape and a_fn returns A(t) (prefetched/bisect in the backtest).

_split_pool partitions every in-process car into exactly one of in-process (t + rem/α <= scope_end), bottleneck (t + rem/α > scope_end), or no-ETA (rem is None), so the self-consistency identity pool_product_cars = inproc + bottleneck + no-ETA holds exactly by construction (F4; already-exited cars in A are out of the pool); the M10 G5 gate re-derives it independently from the backtest JSON, and the dashboard reuses the same static _split_pool as the single source of the pool three-way split.

When the injected guard.status() is not 'FRESH' (STALE stream break), AlertEngine.evaluate returns an empty list and does not advance any Debouncer (STALE freeze, docs/02): no new alerts and no new confirmed level, while the existing level is held for the banner; the production adapter EngineGuardAdapter maps the attribute-style FreshnessGuard (status string) to the engine's .status() protocol (STALE → 'STALE', NORMAL/RECOVERY → 'FRESH').

Each confirmed transition (including the prev_level=None baseline) produces an Alert carrying scope ('day_total'|'shift'), sid ('YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD_day|mid'), t, prev_level, level, delta, gap_n = max(0, target − pred), bottleneck_n, rework_n (bottleneck flag=1 quality rework), blacktop_n (bottleneck flag=2 black-top two-tone, a normal process not quality rework), and sections = the per-section histogram of all bottleneck cars via section_map (missing station → '待确认'); the DDL for dss.work_shift_alert is idempotent and records every confirmed transition without dedup UNIQUE (re-entry after a downgrade appends a new timeline row).

build_station_section bootstraps the full 259-station two-tier station→section map (docs/02 eight-section vocabulary): tier 1 is a prefix code (first 2 chars via PREFIX_MAP, 26 evidence-backed prefixes covering ~163/259 stations), tier 2 is the modal current_process_area per carbody_last_rw_station from dim.dim_vehicle_profile (non-NULL pairs, n >= min_n_profile=3) mapped through the keyword rule kw_section, with tier 2 taking precedence (correcting the prefix); both tiers without evidence yield section='待确认' for user fill-in. The result upserts into dss.dim_station_section with status 'auto'/'confirmed' after user confirmation; backtests never write the dss tables (alerts go only to JSON/MD per the 2026-09-25 decision).

render_alert_line renders one alert line (e.g. '09-12_mid Δ −11.7% red | 缺口 56 台 | 瓶颈 636 台（返修 109 / 黑顶 107 / 主线 …）: 顶涂 210 · 打磨 180 · 前处理 90 …') where mainline = bottleneck_n − rework_n − blacktop_n (constructively consistent), sections are shown Top-3 by count descending, and a shift-scope red alert whose day_total main view is green gets the appended dual-track note '[拆分目标偏置（全天主视图绿，见 F8）]' flagging a possible split-target bias rather than a real gap (day_total red gets no note).

dashboard.active_shifts_at resolves active shifts at t by filtering plan.shift_windows for today AND yesterday with attr_start <= t < end; the previous-day union is what makes cross-day mid shifts resolve correctly (a mid shift with attr 16:30 and end next-day 04:00 still belongs to the previous calendar day, so 09-10 00:00–03:59 matches the 09-09 mid shift). This is the round-1 F-BLK-02 fix: the static _shifts_for_window/is_complete filter is deliberately not used on the online path because it drops a cross-day mid shift inside a 24h dry-run window; a missing plan day yields an empty list without guessing.

build_frame_ctx assembles the per-frame context (isomorphic to the snapshot schema): pool flag distribution over product cars, the three-way pool split via AlertEngine._split_pool with scope_end = active shift end (else next shift end, else all rem-cars are bottleneck), the pred.shift track (A + hit, target from plan_target, grade null before the first anchor work_start+3h), and the pred.day_total track filled only during an active mid shift (A_all over the day-shift window [04:45, t], target = full-day total). render_frame prefixes every frame's first line with '[DSS] ' (the G1 mechanical 288-frame criterion); pre-anchor Δ is displayed as observation progress with the grade suppressed, and replay mode shows 'ETL 诊断不适用·时间穿透' with diagnose null while wall mode shows the real guard.diagnose (F-MED-04/F-MED-05).

write_snapshot writes one JSON per 5-minute round to output/snapshots/{run_tag}/snap_{ts}.json atomically (write a .tmp sibling in the same directory, then os.replace); resolve_run_tag prevents overwriting an existing auto-tag directory by bumping to -r2/-r3 (with a boot-report note) while an explicit DSS_RUN_TAG is treated as an intentional same-directory resume (idempotent append, no -r2). validate_snapshot checks structure only — top-level keys, enums (mode/guard status/levels/anchor_state), nullability, the pool three-way identity (inproc+bottleneck+no_ETA <= size), the exact bottleneck_sections sum, shift.grade null in the pre-anchor state, and replay diagnose null / wall diagnose non-null — with business-value checks left to the post-hoc G2 recomputation gate.

AlertEngine.deb_state(now) is a pure read of the per-scope Debouncer state returning {scope_key: {current_level, pending_level, pending_min}}; it is the only permitted micro-change to the frozen alert_engine.py (docs/07 decision ⑥) and its unit tests pin that it mutates no _deb field (deep-equal before/after) and never calls feed — it exists so the T6 snapshot's alert_state block can record debouncer state even on rounds where alerts is empty.

compute_eta is an independent read-only DB tool (CLI: python -m spike_w3.dashboard --eta <BODY_ID> <TARGET> [--as-of ISO]) that does not read the in-memory pool or depend on the main-loop process; it resolves the latest event (DATE_EVT <= as_of, tie-broken by higher ID) for the current station/flag, returns status='exited' when that event is at an exit station OR a POST_EXIT_STATIONS continuation station (F-R2-01: 76% of exited cars' latest event is at a continuation station), resolves remaining time with the n≥30 discipline (body-type row preferred, else ALL, else an explicit no-estimate error), annotates rework/loop cars (flag 1/2) with a dim_loop_remaining reference, errors explicitly for targets not among the 4 exit stations ('intermediate-station ETA v1 not open, Phase 3 takt-graph shortest path' — never guesses), and routes to the unified engine under DSS_DUAL_RING=1.

make_t6_hook returns the per-round hook closure installed as round_hook on the 01_boot_online main loop (after each run_one_round): it resolves the active shift via active_shifts_at, computes the shared pool view once, advances the AlphaTracker only in on mode (update then read committed), calls engine.evaluate (STALE → []), assembles build_frame_ctx, writes the snapshot, and renders the frame via the sink. build_t6_components assembles the production components (tables/comp_excl/section_map/engine, tracker only when alpha_mode=on) and resolves the run tag; 01_boot_online.main wires the hook when DSS_CONSOLE is on (default), and a failed console assembly prints a warning without blocking the main loop; DSS_CONSOLE=0 (hook None) leaves the loop byte-identical to the frozen T2.6 behavior.

02_shadow_replay.run_rolling accepts an alert_hook parameter that defaults to None (zero production impact: M9 behavior byte-for-byte unchanged); when supplied it is invoked every 5-minute step with (cur, pool, conn, tables, comp_excl, cfg_m9, [active_shift] or []) and its returned serialized alerts accumulate into the run_rolling result. The M10 driver 03_alert_backtest.make_hook builds exactly such a hook reusing run_rolling + _pool_view, and its gates are G0 unit tests, G1 day-total accuracy (21:30 anchor, median ≤5pp + zero red), G1b engine pred == M9 pred_off@5h, G2 level == grade(Δ), G3 advance ≥2h, G4 no confirmed transition in the [anchor−10min, anchor) window (transition count demoted to the observation item G4_obs per the 2026-09-26 decision B), G5 pool identity, G6 full 21-scope-day coverage.

The M9 gates() pure function judges acceptance per alpha_mode: G1 (alpha=off engine consistency, both modes) = per-shift |roll−static| ≤ min(p3_inproc, 25)+2 with the p3_inproc ≤ 25 hard cap AND full-factory and mid-shift 5h relative medians within 0.5pp of the static reference (relative gate, not a hardcoded absolute baseline); in off mode (production default) G2 = off-median ≤ 10% absolute line, G3 = True (α not enabled), G4 = False with main-side soft handling (not blocking when G1–G3 pass and DSS_G4_HARD is unset); in on mode G2/G3/G4 use the α=on medians (on ≤ off, mid on < off strictly).

The focused test surface is fully synthetic (offline): tests/test_w3_predictor.py pins rem_of/a_of/predict (alpha=1 vs alpha=1.2, stale-still-counted, non-product exclusion, tz TypeError) under DSS_DUAL_RING=0 + DSS_USE_NET_DELAY=0 (unified-engine rem_of semantics live in tests/test_w4_engine_wiring.py); tests/test_w3_alpha.py covers build_takt_baseline P50/fallback and the full AlphaTracker lifecycle; tests/test_w3_m9.py covers the gates() pure function with each gate flipped independently; tests/test_w3_alert.py covers split_target/grade/Debouncer, the dual-scope engine (union double-count regression, F10 window, STALE freeze, flag layering, identity, deb_state pure-read); tests/test_w3_dashboard.py / test_w3_snapshot.py / test_w3_eta_menu.py cover frame rendering (five states, pre/post-anchor grade gating, replay banner), snapshot schema/atomic write/tag anti-overwrite, and the seven-branch compute_eta; tests/test_w3_t64_hook.py covers the T6.4 hook (call order, STALE round, deb_state regression).

Every entry point in the T3/T4/T6 chain enforces the shared timezone discipline: naive datetimes raise TypeError at rem_of/a_of/predict/obs_window/AlphaTracker.update/AlertEngine.evaluate/Debouncer.feed/active_shifts_at/build_frame_ctx/write_snapshot/compute_eta, on the Asia/Shanghai baseline (single DSN with SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Shanghai'), machine-enforced rather than documented-only; the W2/W1/T2 upstream files remain zero-change (predictor/alert_engine reference them read-only via importlib).
